answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through stake-backed identity. Each participant locks a collateral bond and needs two distinct peers to vouch, each risking their own stake. A violet cluster sharing one funder triggers audits that slash proven fakes' bonds and punish their vouchers. The trusted harbor therefore demands real, separable capital, not just new names. On the tundra of clones, an attacker must fund a fresh bond and recruit independent guarantors per shell, so each identity costs more than the last and farming becomes a guaranteed loss.
